name: application-order-status-tracker
title: Order Status Tracker
description: Horizontal shipment status stepper — Placed, Shipped, Out for delivery, Delivered — with a date under each stage and a computed completed/current/upcoming state.
useWhen: Showing the progress of a single linear order/shipment through a fixed sequence of stages.
Each stage benefits from a date so users know both what happened and when.
Pairing with `checkout-order-summary` or an order-detail page to communicate delivery status at a glance.
avoidWhen: The sequence isn't linear or a stage can be skipped/repeated — a stepper implies a fixed forward-only path.
You need a generic multi-step form/onboarding flow, not an order's real-world status — use `steps` or `stepper-wizard` instead.
You're tracking many orders in a list, not one order in detail — a status badge in a table row is lighter weight than a full stepper per row.
responsiveBehavior: Steps share equal flex-1 width in a single row; on very narrow viewports the labels may need to wrap or the component should switch to a vertical stack via a variant.
accessibility: Steps are list items in an <ol> with an aria-label describing the tracker's purpose, so the sequence and count are conveyed to assistive tech.
The current step carries aria-current="step" in addition to its visual highlight.
Completed vs. upcoming states are distinguished by both icon (checkmark vs. empty dot) and label weight, not by color alone.
Estimated (not yet occurred) dates are visually deemphasized relative to confirmed dates, communicating certainty through contrast, not implying a factual date has passed.

variants.title: Order Status Tracker
variants.description: Four-stage tracker with Placed and Shipped complete, Out for delivery current, and Delivered upcoming with an estimated date.
accessibility: Step state (complete/current/upcoming) is computed from a single currentStepIndex, so it always stays internally consistent.

variants.title: Order Status Tracker (Dark)
variants.description: Order status tracker adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Connector line and icon colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
